Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Australia's reply. The English players are seen going through some last-minute fielding drills before striding out to the center. Australia's two openers Usman Khawaja and David Warner make their way out to the middle now. Stuart Broad has the new ball in hand for England and is raring to go. Let's play...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

England have declared at a score of 393-8! It seems like the hosts want to test out the Australian openers who have been in the field for 78 overs. This is what Bazball offers us! No one here would have expected this to happen more so the Australians who would have not been prepared to face the new ball for 20 odd minutes. England started off looking to pile on the score from the word go but lost Ben Duckett early. A 70-run partnership between Ollie Pope and Zak Crawley got them moving with Crawley scoring 61 runs in 73 deliveries. Harry Brook looked to keep the scoreboard ticking but was unfortunately dismissed on 32 and Ben Stokes did not trouble the scorers much. Jonny Bairstow scored 78 in as many balls to add the required impetus to the inning but he looked to play one shot too many. Moeen Ali and Stuart Broad looked to throw their bats at the ball and perished but Ollie Robinson stood by Joe Root till he reached his century. Nathan Lyon was expensive but claimed four crucial wickets for Australia with Josh Hazlewood chipping in with two and Scott Boland along with Cameron Green claimed one each.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session on Day 1. The Australian players make their way out the middle followed by the two English batters. Joe Root and Jonny Bairstow will resume the innings for England. Scott Boland will start the proceedings with the ball for Australia. Off we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Australia have tried to bowl testing lines and lengths but have found very little help from this wicket. That has not hindered them in getting breakthroughs at crucial intervals and have been chipping away at the wickets right through the day. They have tried to spread the field out to negate the attacking intent shown by the hosts but in the process have allowed an easy rotation of strike. Nathan Lyon got a lucky wicket against the run of play and broke a partnership that seemed to building nicely. Josh Hazlewood continued to impress on his comeback as he claimed the wicket of the England skipper. They have shuffled around with the bowlers and despite having claimed five wickets, they would like to put a cap on the scoring rate. Will they be able to run through England’s long batting order in the final session? Or will the hosts continue to score freely without losing wickets? Do join us at 8.30 pm IST (3 pm GMT) for the third and final session of Day 1 and see how it plays out.

SESSION SUMMARY - 116 runs, 25.2 overs, 2 wickets. Another session that could have easily belonged to England if it was not for the two wickets that fell in consecutive overs to keep the tie in Australia’s favor. Despite losing a wicket just before Lunch, Joe Root and Harry Brook started with positive intent as they added 51 runs in 64 deliveries for the fourth wicket. Brook was dismissed in an extraordinary manner as the ball lobbed up into the air off his pads and then landed on footmarks on the crease to go onto the stumps. Things got worse for them as they lost their skipper Ben Stokes in the very next over chasing a wide one and Australia looked to be well ahead at that point. Joe Root continued to hold up one end with a half-century and is on 66 not out as he has begun rebuilding the innings along with Jonny Bairstow who is unbeaten on 33 runs. They will hope to continue the good work and will know that they bat deep so will not be worried about the number of wickets they have lost.

They will have a spring in their step after claiming a wicket just before the break. Joe Root is joined by Harry Brook and they will look to build a partnership. The question everyone had in their minds before the first ball was how will 'Bazball' stand up against Australia. After Ben Stokes won the toss and opted to put runs on the board, Zak Crawley seemed to have answered that question by smacking the first ball of the Test for a boundary. He, along with Ben Duckett got England off to a swift start. The latter departed to a false shot after which Ollie Pope joined hands with Zak Crawley and kept the scoreboard ticking with a 70-run stand. Just when both batters were looking at ease in the middle, Pope paid the price for playing across the line. Despite his departure, Joe Root and Zak Crawley kept the runs flowing for England. However, the latter's departure has meant that the English middle order will have their work cut out in the second session. Can Australia continue to chip in with wickets in the second session or will see counter-attacking batting from England? We will find out as the play resumes in the second session at 6.10 pm IST (12.40 pm GMT).

SESSION SUMMARY - 124 runs, 26.4 overs, 3 wickets. The wicket of Zak Crawley at the stroke of Lunch has tilted the first session in Australia's favor! Riding high on confidence after a sensational bowling effort in the WTC final, Australia were put under the pump early by the two English openers. They did manage to dry up the boundaries after dismissing Ben Duckett but the plan by Pat Cummins to bowl with an open field allowed the opposition batters to release the pressure. As he has done so often, Nathan Lyon provided Australia with a much-needed breakthrough by trapping Pope in front of the stumps. That said, Australia failed to pick an edge when Crawley was on 40 but Scott Boland made up for it by dismissing him in the final over before Lunch. On a belter of a wicket at Edgbaston, Australia will be delighted that they have sent England's top three back in the hut.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Australia get a crucial wicket right at the stroke of Lunch! Scott Boland bowls this slightly back of a length and just outside the off stump. He gets a bit of extra bounce and nips away from the batter as Zak Crawley looks to feel for this. There is a clear deviation but the umpire remains unmoved despite the celebrations and the appeal from the Australian players. Zak Crawley also stands his ground and after some discussion, Pat Cummins goes upstairs for the review. UltraEdge confirms that the ball clips the glove of the batter as it goes through to Alex Carey who takes a simple catch. The on-field decision has to be reversed and England have lost their third wicket. Zak Crawley has to depart after a well-made half-century but he will be disappointed that he was unable to go into the break with his wicket intact.

We are moments away from the start of the game but first, the two teams will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Australia first followed by England's national anthem.

Pat Cummins, the captain of Australia, says that they would have batted first as well. Informs that Mitchell Starc makes way for Josh Hazlewood. Adds that it was a tough call but it is good to have Hazlewood come in. Mentions that it is a good problem to have and it is important to manage workloads. Reckons that the WTC final was a good preparation and they are eager now to go here.

Ben Stokes, the skipper of England, starts by informing that they will bat first. Adds that it looks like a good cricket wicket and feels that it is a good toss to win. Mentions that he feels proud of all the hype that has been around and it is a special moment for him and the team. On Moeen Ali, he says that it is great to have him back. Shares that it was an unfortunate injury to Jack Leach. Adds that Moeen Ali has produced unbelievable performances and they know what he can bring to the team.

Having recently lifted the 2021-23 World Test Championship mace, Australia come into this series high on confidence and do start as slight favourites to retain the Ashes urn. However, they will be wary of England’s record at home, and they will need to be at their best in this series. The visitors seem to have all bases covered, and the return of Josh Hazlewood bolsters their pace attack even more. Can Australia be successful in countering England's ruthlessness? Let’s find out. In the previous edition of the Ashes held Down Under, England suffered a tough 4-0 loss and will be eager to return the favour this time around. That said, the ‘Bazball' approach under the captaincy of Ben Stokes has worked wonders for them, but they now face their toughest test against Australia. The batting unit has immense depth, and it is the bowling department that lacks Test match fitness.
